data.G: Research pending. Keep the valid measured baseline (commit b24602f5af40d7501681193ba190461e3d15e3c5) as the initial candidate; do not integrate unmeasured changes.
data.analysis: Choose N=3: the supplied valid baseline averages 46.67 µs (three samples) and, for n=2^22, its source launches four 128-thread reduction stages followed by a device copy. The source also uses shared-memory synchronization in each stage; these are plausible optimization opportunities, not measured bottleneck attribution. The three objectives separately investigate large-input hierarchical reduction, small-input launch reduction, and a large-input initialized-atomic alternative. Only the baseline has measurements; require correctness and repeated performance measurements for candidates, then independently confirm the final integration. Consulted the official CUDA 12.6.3 Programming Guide and matching Best Practices Guide: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.6.3/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html and https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.6.3/cuda-c-best-practices-guide/index.html.

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, explore a large-input two-stage reduction: have CTAs read coalesced, disjoint tiles, accumulate multiple values per thread, reduce within each CTA, and write one partial to bounded scratch; have a final kernel reduce those partials directly to out. Tune tile and block configuration for n=4194304. Cover arbitrary legal sizes without overreads, preserve exact int32 results and the ABI/default stream, and retain a correct fallback for sizes outside this path. Compare correctness on all checks and repeated performance against the baseline.
children.subject: Large-input hierarchical reduction with fewer stages

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, explore a generic size-based single-CTA reduction that writes its result directly to out for genuinely small inputs, eliminating intermediate partials and the final device copy where beneficial. Measure crossover thresholds rather than hardcoding test sizes; retain an appropriate fallback for larger inputs and keep every legal size correct, with bounded reads and exact int32 output. Compare all correctness checks and repeated timings.
children.subject: Small-input direct-output reduction and launch reduction

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, evaluate a large-input alternative with an ordered output-zeroing kernel followed by a multi-CTA grid-stride reduction; each CTA reduces its own values and performs one int32 atomicAdd to out. Tune CTA count/work per CTA to balance input throughput against contention. Do not rely on initialized scratch or unsafe inter-block initialization. Preserve exact results, bounds, ABI, default-stream ordering, and a correct fallback for other legal sizes; compare all checks and repeated timings against the baseline and hierarchical approach.
children.subject: Large-input atomic final aggregation
